sha256_tree: use git-style normalized mode for host-agnostic hashing

The previous implementation hashed the raw stat.st_mode, which embeds the local umask into every tree hash. A clone made with umask 0002 would produce a hash different from one made with umask 0022 even though the file contents are byte-identical. This is the root cause of the pre-existing test_mirror_integrity failure seen on fresh clones.

Fix: _portable_mode() clamps to 0o100644 for regular files, 0o100755 if any execute bit is set (git's own canonicalisation). Tree hashes are now reproducible across any Linux/macOS/WSL host regardless of umask, cluster permissions, or tar preservation.

Validation: on this worktree all 673 tree hashes match the stored catalog values without touching any catalog JSON. The test_all_skills_are_physically_mirrored_and_documented test now passes for the first time on a fresh clone.

validate_catalog: refactor to _collect_entry_errors; sequential by default after measured regression from threads

Measured wall-clock on 673-entry catalog:
- sequential: 3.95 s (3 runs avg)
- ThreadPoolExecutor cpu*2 workers: 9.14 s (2.3x regression)
- ThreadPoolExecutor 8 workers: 9.57 s
The per-entry validation is dominated by pure-Python string/dict work (GIL-bound) with only brief hashlib segments; pool dispatch of ~673 tiny tasks dwarfs the <1 ms work unit. Kept the _collect_entry_errors refactor and threadpool path behind an opt-in VALIDATE_CATALOG_MAX_WORKERS env var for future I/O-bound workloads.

AI commit identity: immutable enforcement rule

Every commit produced by an AI agent in this repository must use Author =
Committer = 'AI agent' with an empty email, and any AI co-author trailer
must be 'Co-authored-by: AI agent' with no email. Human contributors keep
their real GitHub identities. The full rule set lives at the top of
AGENTS.md.
